skill.name: connecting-to-logseq
skill.description: Guides secure connections to Logseq graphs through the local HTTP API, Logseq CLI, or MCP server, including configuration and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Configure, test, and troubleshoot local Logseq connections across HTTP, CLI, and MCP backends.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, loopback addresses, documented database names, and targeted environment access. Confirmed issues include unpinned package or script execution and a command that prints the API token. Unsafe write defaults and advice to disable host protections create additional high-risk concerns.

remediation.issue: Write confirmation and backups are disabled in both example configurations.
remediation.suggestion: Set both safeguards to true and require explicit user approval before every graph write.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting tells users to print LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN.
remediation.suggestion: Replace direct output with a presence-only test and redact credentials from all logs.

remediation.issue: Instructions execute unpinned npm packages and unaudited local scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, include audited scripts, verify integrity, and request confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Windows troubleshooting recommends elevation and disabling antivirus.
remediation.suggestion: Remove these steps and provide least-privilege firewall, port, and log diagnostics instead.

semantic_findings.description: The example configuration disables write confirmation and backups while the documented HTTP and MCP backends support full writes. Unapproved changes could damage graph data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both configuration examples explicitly set confirmWrites and backupBeforeWrite to false. The backend table states that HTTP and MCP provide full write access.

content.user_title: Connect Claude and Codex to Logseq
content.value_statement: Connecting an AI assistant to Logseq requires choosing and configuring the correct backend. This skill provides focused setup, request, and troubleshooting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Compares HTTP API, CLI, and MCP backend requirements.
Explains how to enable Logseq developer mode and create an API token.
Documents local HTTP requests in Python, JavaScript, and cURL.
Shows CLI queries, graph exports, validation, and in-app access.
Describes environment variables, graph paths, and backend configuration.
Diagnoses connection, authentication, CLI, query, and MCP errors.
limitations: HTTP and MCP access require a running Logseq instance with its API enabled.
The package contains guidance only; referenced setup scripts and MCP server files are absent.
CLI write support is limited, and query attributes differ between graph formats.
The skill cannot verify tokens, paths, or connectivity without permission to run local commands.

use_cases.title: Connect a personal graph
use_cases.description: Set up a local HTTP connection for reading and updating a personal Logseq graph.

use_cases.title: Automate graph queries
use_cases.description: Choose CLI commands for offline queries, exports, validation, or continuous integration.

use_cases.title: Repair an integration
use_cases.description: Trace authentication, port, graph path, query, or MCP startup failures.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Logseq backend for my needs. I need [read or write access], and Logseq is [running or offline].

prompt_templates.title: Set up local HTTP access
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through enabling Logseq HTTP access and storing the API token without printing or committing it.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Logseq connection error: [error]. Ask before running commands and do not reveal credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Design an automated workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Logseq automation for [goal] using [CLI, HTTP, or MCP]. Include permissions, backups, confirmations, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Which backend supports offline batch queries?
output_examples.output: Use the Logseq CLI with a local graph path. It supports offline queries and exports, but write operations are limited.

output_examples.input: My local API returns an authentication error.
output_examples.output: Confirm that the API is enabled and the token variable is present. Create a new token if needed, without displaying its value.

output: Enable the local Logseq API and create a dedicated token.
Build and configure the MCP server only after reviewing its dependencies.
Require confirmation and backup before every write operation.

best_practices: Keep the API bound to localhost and never expose its port publicly.
Store tokens in environment variables and test only whether each variable exists.
Require confirmation and a current backup before modifying graph data.
anti_patterns: Do not print API tokens in terminal output or assistant transcripts.
Do not disable antivirus or run Logseq with elevated privileges for routine troubleshooting.
Do not execute unpinned packages or unaudited setup scripts automatically.

faq.question: Which backend should I use?
faq.answer: Use HTTP for live access, CLI for offline automation, and MCP for assistant tool integration.

faq.question: Does Logseq need to be running?
faq.answer: HTTP and MCP require Logseq to run. Direct CLI access to a local graph can work offline.

faq.question: Where should I store the API token?
faq.answer: Store it in a protected environment variable. Never place the real token in source files or command output.

faq.question: Can this skill update my graph?
faq.answer: The HTTP and MCP backends support writes. Require explicit approval and create a backup before any change.

faq.question: Are the referenced scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package includes documentation and an example configuration, but not the referenced scripts or MCP server.

faq.question: Does the skill support both Logseq graph formats?
faq.answer: Yes, but CLI capabilities and Datalog attributes differ between database and Markdown graphs.
